overview.title: Surf Village North of Agadir
overview.p1: Taghazout is the surf village that sits just north of Agadir’s resort sprawl. The vibe shifts: fewer high-rises, more boards on rooftops, cafés that open to the sound of the Atlantic. Reef breaks attract surfers year-round; non-surfers still come for the village scale and coastal walks.
overview.p2: A half-day is enough for lunch and a look; a full day works if you take a lesson or simply sit with the ocean. Agree taxi fares before leaving Agadir, or book a transfer.
overview.p3: It is an easy add-on to an Agadir base and a calmer contrast to the main bay’s hotel strip.

food.title: Village cafés
food.p1: Taghazout’s cafés serve simple food, smoothies and the post-surf ritual of sitting still.
food.p2: Village dining is casual — for a big seafood feast, Agadir’s port still competes.

q1.question: Do I need to surf to enjoy it?
q1.answer: No — the village and coast are enough for a relaxed visit.

q2.question: How far from Agadir?
q2.answer: About 20–30 minutes by road depending on traffic.

q3.question: Can beginners take lessons?
q3.answer: Yes — several schools operate; book licensed instructors.

q4.question: Do I need a guide at Taghazout?
q4.answer: Optional for a simple visit; useful for context and timing.

q5.question: Is Taghazout suitable for families?
q5.answer: Yes in most cases with normal supervision.
